sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia. Srinagar (1585m) is the summer capital of Jammu & Kashmir. Best season Apr–Oct; accessible year-round by air but cold Dec–Feb. All records needs_review.

places.name: Dal Lake
places.description: Srinagar's defining 18 sq km Himalayan lake, lined with Mughal gardens and the traditional wooden houseboat colonies that have defined Kashmiri tourism for over a century. Shikara (wooden gondola) rides at dawn and dusk are the quintessential experience. A floating vegetable market operates pre-sunrise. The lake is a UNESCO tentative World Heritage Site and the heart of Srinagar life.
places.openingDays: Open all day; shikara operators available dawn–dusk

places.name: Shalimar Bagh
places.description: Mughal pleasure garden built by Emperor Jahangir for his wife Nur Jahan in 1619, on the northeast shore of Dal Lake. The classic terraced chaharbagh design features three rising chinar-tree-shaded terraces with cascading fountains and the Black Marble pavilion. Among the best-preserved Mughal gardens in India; UNESCO World Heritage tentative list. Spring and autumn are the finest visiting seasons.

places.name: Nishat Bagh
places.description: The second-largest Mughal garden in Kashmir (1633), designed by Nur Jahan's brother Asif Khan on twelve terraces against the Zabarwan Hills. The name means Garden of Delight. Chinar trees provide dense shade and spectacular autumn colour (late October). Slightly south of Shalimar Bagh; often visited together on a Dal Lake garden circuit.

places.name: Chashme Shahi
places.description: The smallest of the three major Mughal gardens (1632), built by Ali Mardan Khan under Shah Jahan around a natural spring whose water is reputed to have medicinal properties. Set against the Zabarwan Hills with excellent views of Dal Lake below. The garden has three terraces with a cool natural spring channel. Less crowded than Shalimar or Nishat; a short visit.

places.name: Shankaracharya Temple
places.description: Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, perched on Shankaracharya Hill (1100m) above Srinagar. 243 steps from the car park to the summit. The hilltop commands the best 360° panoramic view of the Kashmir Valley — Dal Lake, the Jhelum River plain, and snow peaks. The original temple is ancient (6th century BCE according to tradition); the current stone structure is more recent. Evening light is outstanding.

places.name: Jama Masjid Srinagar
places.description: Srinagar's largest mosque, founded in 1394 by Sultan Sikandar and rebuilt several times. The current structure has 378 wooden columns of deodar cedar, each made from a single tree. Courtyard capacity of 33,333 worshippers. Set in the heart of the old city near Nowhatta chowk; Friday prayers draw immense crowds. Non-Muslim visitors are welcome outside prayer times.

places.name: Hazratbal Shrine
places.description: The most important Muslim shrine in Kashmir, on the northwest shore of Dal Lake. Said to contain Moi-e-Muqqadas — a hair relic of the Prophet Muhammad — in the central white-domed mosque. The Friday congregation is the largest in the valley. Huge pilgrimage numbers on Islamic festivals. Non-Muslim visitors may view the exterior and grounds; the relic is only occasionally displayed.

places.name: Hari Parbat Fort
places.description: 18th-century Afghan-era fort atop Hari Parbat hill (1500m), visible from across Srinagar. Built on a site sacred to both Hindus (Sharika Devi temple inside) and Sikhs (Gurdwara Chatti Padshahi on the south slope). The fort walls enclose the hill; entry requires prior permission from ASI or J&K Tourism. The views of Dal Lake and the old city are among Srinagar's best.

places.name: Pari Mahal
places.description: Ruins of a 17th-century Sufi school (Dara Shikoh's observatory-garden) in seven terraces on the southern slope of the Zabarwan Hills, above Chashme Shahi. The arched terraces frame views of Dal Lake. Less visited than the Mughal gardens; a quiet heritage picnic spot. Combine with Chashme Shahi immediately below. Maintained by ASI.

places.name: Khanqah Shah-i-Hamadan
places.description: 14th-century Sufi khanqah (hospice) of Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani, the missionary credited with introducing Islam to Kashmir in 1372. The existing wooden structure dates to the late 17th century with intricate papier-mâché and woodwork decoration. On the Jhelum River bank in the old city; non-Muslim visitors may view from outside. One of the oldest Muslim buildings in Kashmir.
places.openingDays: Daily 07:00–20:00 (outer courtyard; non-Muslim visitors exterior only)

places.name: Lal Chowk
places.description: Srinagar's central commercial square and political hub, the city's traditional market heart. The surrounding lanes — Residency Road, Maulana Azad Road, Boulevard Road — have traditional Kashmiri craft shops selling papier-mâché, Pashmina shawls, silk carpets, walnut woodwork and dried fruits. The Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar) at the centre is the city's most iconic landmark.

places.name: Nagin Lake
places.description: Smaller and quieter lake to the northwest of Dal Lake, connected to it by a canal. Often described as cleaner and calmer than Dal; the houseboat community here is more low-key and less tourist-saturated. Popular for kayaking, canoeing and early morning shikara rides without the crowds. Particularly peaceful in the early morning when the water is still.

places.name: Srinagar Wazwan Feast
places.description: Wazwan is the grand Kashmiri multi-course feast of 36 dishes, prepared by wazas (specialist cooks). Essential dishes: rogan josh (lamb in Kashmiri chilli), gushtaba (meatballs in yoghurt gravy), yakhni (aromatic lamb in yoghurt), and tabak maaz (rib rack). Preeti Restaurant and Ahdoos are the safest bets for tourists.

places.name: Srinagar Noon Chai and Sheermal
places.description: Noon chai (pink Kashmiri salt tea brewed with gunpowder tea leaves, milk, and baking soda) is a cultural staple. Served with sheermal (saffron-flavoured flatbread) or kulcha. A ritual morning or evening drink in Kashmiri homes — available at traditional bakeries in the old city.
